title: How Much Would It Cost To Run House's Team in Real Life?
description:
Gregory House ran an entire hospital department that existed only to solve the cases no other doctor could crack, and he did it while breaking nearly every rule in the building. When a businessman called it a three-million-dollar black hole, it raised a fascinating question. In this video, we calculate the real-life cost of running House’s team from the ground up, every phase, every expense, every dollar it takes to keep a genius who gets sued more than anyone in the hospital.

We break it all down. The department built around one tenured, impossible-to-fire diagnostician and his rotating team of fellows. The endless tests, week-long ICU stays, and the private investigator smuggled onto the books as a broken coffee machine. The lawsuits that make House’s tiny team responsible for 40 percent of the hospital’s legal cases. And the price of keeping him, the MRI he destroyed, the clinic hours he never worked, and the hundred-million-dollar donor he cost Cuddy her funding. Add it up and House’s department runs north of 105 million dollars, but almost none of it is the team. Was the businessman right, or is House worth every penny?
